query: 浸没式光刻的缺陷为什么老是集中在晶圆边缘?把书里的机理链条和缓解措施给我捋一遍。
source_id: Principles of Lithography, Fourth Edition (Harry J. Levinson)
gold_standard: 机理链:浸没液并不局限在曝光区域,而是延伸到远超曝光面积的范围 → 浸液会从晶圆边缘或工件台表面拾取颗粒 → 晶圆边缘有倒角,浸液还会进入晶圆与吸盘之间的小缝隙,把晶圆背面的颗粒也带起来 → 这些颗粒再沉积到晶圆上造成缺陷、降低良率。缓解措施:把晶圆下沉嵌入吸盘使晶圆顶面与工件台面齐平以改善边缘扫描;保持晶圆背面和边缘清洁对浸没光刻至关重要;对边缘胶去除(edge-bead removal)质量的要求也因浸没而更高。
success_criteria: 完整复现『浸液越界→拾取边缘/台面颗粒→吸入晶圆-吸盘缝隙带上背面颗粒→沉积成缺陷』链条,并给出晶圆嵌入吸盘与背面/边缘清洁两条措施。
evidence: --[p441]-- The introduction of immersion lithography has led to an increased focus on wafer-edge defects in particular. The immersion fluid extends well beyond the area being exposed. As a consequence, the fluid can pick up particles from the wafer edge or wafer stage. Because wafers are beveled, particles from the back side of the wafer can even be picked up from fluid in the small gap between the wafer and the chuck. --[p441]-- To address scanning at the wafer edge, the wafer is recessed into the chuck so that the tops of the wafer and the stage are at the same level (see Fig. 10.5). Fluid will go into the small gap between the wafer and the chuck and pick up particles. These particles can be deposited on the wafer, reducing yield. Keeping wafers clean on the back side and edges is important for immersion lithography. --[p87]-- The use of immersion lithography, which is discussed in more detail in Chapter 10, injects additional motivation for a high-quality edge-bead-removal process.

query: 掩模为什么一定要贴 pellicle?到了浸没式光刻(NA>1)它又惹出了什么新麻烦?把原理和新问题分开讲清楚。
source_id: Principles of Lithography, Fourth Edition (Harry J. Levinson)
gold_standard: 原理:曝光期间颗粒难免落在掩模上,贴上约 1 μm 厚的聚合物薄膜后,颗粒落在离图形面几毫米的 pellicle 或玻璃背面处,在远小于 1 μm 的典型焦深下完全离焦,不再成像为可印缺陷。新问题(浸没、NA>1):掩模侧入射角最大可达 arcsin(NA/N),0.93-NA 4 倍镜头即达 13.4 度;NA>1 时 pellicle 透过率随入射角变化,等效引入切趾(apodization),使线宽随 pitch 变化,透射光的相位也随入射角变化。此外薄 pellicle 可减小折射与球差类波前误差,Teflon AF2400 在 193 nm 折射率约 1.35。
success_criteria: 原理侧给出『颗粒远离焦面所以不成像』;问题侧给出 NA>1 下透过率随角度变化→切趾→线宽随 pitch 变化,并提及 13.4 度(0.93 NA/4×)的典型角度。
evidence: --[p334]-- To avoid new printable defects, pellicles are attached to photomasks. Pellicles are thin (1 m) polymer films stretched across a frame that is attached to the mask. --[p334]-- Particles deposited on the pelliclized photomask fall onto the pellicle or glass backside of the mask, and are therefore several millimeters away from the patterned mask features that are being imaged. With small depths-of-field, these particles are not going to be in focus. --[p337]-- For a 0.93-NA 4 lens, angles can be as large as 13.4 deg. --[p338]-- However, at numerical apertures >1.0 relevant to immersion lithography (see Chapter 10), the pellicle's transmission varies with angle of incidence, effectively inducing apodization and causing linewidths to vary (Fig. 7.28) as a function of pitch (among other consequences). There will also be differences in phase of the transmitted rays as a function of the angle of incidence.

query: 为什么波长降到 193 nm 以下,EUV 的镜片和掩模就全都必须改成反射式了?多层膜反射镜又是靠什么在近正入射下做到高反射的?把逻辑链讲完整。
source_id: Principles of Lithography, Fourth Edition (Harry J. Levinson)
gold_standard: 逻辑链:(1) 波长显著低于 193 nm 时,所有已知材料都因吸收太强而无法制作有效的折射光学元件,且均质材料在近正入射下的反射率都极低;(2) 波长 <50 nm 时所有材料折射率≈1,单界面难以产生高反射,只有掠入射除外;(3) 出路是多层膜:高低 Z 材料交替沉积、满足 Bragg 条件,每个界面的小反射率叠加,在近正入射做到 60–70% 反射;(4) Mo/Si 多层膜中 Mo 层约 3 nm、Si 层约 4 nm,反射峰约 13.4 nm,插入 B4C 层后在 13.5 nm 达 70%;(5) 因此 EUV 中不仅透镜全反射,掩模也必须是反射式,且没有高透过材料可用。
success_criteria: 按序答出:材料全吸收→n≈1 单界面反射不足→多层膜 Bragg 叠加 60–70%→Mo/Si 层厚 ~3/~4 nm 与 13.5 nm 波长→掩模同样必须反射;至少覆盖其中四环。
evidence: --[p493]-- As the wavelength of light decreases significantly below 193 nm, all known materials become too absorbing to be used for fabricating effectual refractive optical elements. Moreover, at such short wavelengths the reflectivity of all homogenous materials becomes very small, at least at the near-normal angles of incidence relevant to high-resolution imaging optics. --[p494]-- At wavelengths <50 nm, all materials have indices of refraction ≈1. Thus, it is difficult to create high reflectance from a single interface, except at grazing angles of incidence. At EUV wavelengths, it has proven possible to make mirrors with moderate reflectivity at near-normal angles of incidence, in the range of 60-70%, by the use of coatings comprising multiple layers. --[p495]-- For Mo/Si multilayers designed for near-normal reflectance, the molybdenum layers are ~3 nm thick, while the silicon layers are ~4 nm thick. --[p493]-- For EUV lithography, not only must all optical elements in the lens be reflecting, so must be the mask.

query: 按书里 pellicle 防颗粒的最小间距公式算一下:4 倍缩倍、0.93 NA 的机台上,颗粒直径 90 μm,最小 standoff 要多大?再考虑书上说的那个『只保护一半』的修正呢?
source_id: Principles of Lithography, Fourth Edition (Harry J. Levinson)
gold_standard: 式(7.4) t = 4Md/NA:t = 4×4×90 μm/0.93 ≈ 1548 μm ≈ 1.55 mm。书中指出更精细的理论研究表明成像只受到式(7.4)给出值约一半颗粒尺寸的保护,对应有效保护能力约减半(≈0.77 mm 量级的等效裕度);作为对照,书中提到 standoff 6.3 mm、颗粒 <90 μm 时工艺窗口不会明显缩小。
success_criteria: 给出 t=4Md/NA 的代入过程并算出 ≈1.5–1.6 mm;能补充『保护能力约为公式值一半』的修正结论。
evidence: --[p335]-- Early theoretical studies showed that image intensities are not affected by amounts greater than 10% as long as the pellicle standoff is at least as large as t = 4Md/NA (7.4) --[p335]-- where M is the lens reduction, NA is the numerical aperture of the lens, and d is the diameter of the particle on the pellicle. More detailed theoretical investigations have shown that imaging is protected for particles only about one half of that given by Eq. (7.4). --[p335]-- For example, process windows are not reduced significantly with pellicle standoff distances of 6.3 mm and particles <90 μm.

query: 浸没光刻里激光被水吸收发热:NA 1.35 时最斜光线在水里走多长?水升温 1°C 造成的相位误差算出来多大?这个误差要不要紧?
source_id: Principles of Lithography, Fourth Edition (Harry J. Levinson)
gold_standard: 分三步:(1) 由 NA = n·sinΘ = 1.35、n = 1.437(水在 193 nm 的折射率)得 Θ = 70°;(2) 发热被限制在晶圆表面 200 nm 内的水层,最斜光线路径 = 200 nm/cos70° ≈ 584 nm;(3) 水折射率温度系数约 −1×10⁻⁴/°C(ArF),1°C 温升的相位误差 = n×(−1×10⁻⁴/°C)×584 nm ≈ −0.0839 nm。判断:其他像差的相位误差典型约 1 nm,单场曝光内水发热引入的相位误差不算关键,但整片曝光过程水平均水温会升高,因此浸液必须循环并主动控温。
success_criteria: 三个中间结果齐全:θ=70°、路径 584 nm、相位误差 ≈−0.0839 nm(±10% 内判对),并给出『单场不关键、整片需循环控温』的结论。
evidence: --[p440]-- the heat appears to be confined to a volume of water within 200 nm of the wafer surface during exposure. Suppose that we are considering a lens with a numerical aperture of 1.35. In this case, NA = n sinΘ = 1.35. Thus, θ = 70 deg assuming n = 1.437, the value appropriate for water at a wavelength of 193 nm. The path through which the most oblique angles will have a path length through the volume of heated water of 200 nm/cosθ = 584 nm (10.9). Consequently, a 1°C temperature rise within this volume will create a phase error of n(1°C)(−1×10⁻⁴/°C)584 nm = −0.0839 nm (10.10). --[p440]-- Since phase errors from other aberrations are typically ~1 nm, the additional phase errors induced by water heating are not considered critical during the exposure of a single field. Over the course of exposing an entire wafer, the average water temperature could rise, so the immersion fluid must be circulated, and temperature must be controlled actively.
